steps: UI: test wallet m4Ac… (the DAO authority) on #/treasury: 10, Swap SOL for VTR (buy_tokens; it adds 10 voting power and moves no SOL or tokens)
UI: #/create, title and summary, Broadcast Proposal (proposal "UI proposal 06006")
UI: Finalize & Pick Winner on that proposal after its 40 s vote (nobody voted, so it was rejected for no quorum)
UI (second run, voting period 150 s): Swap SOL for VTR, 10 more
UI: All Proposals, open it, Yes, Confirm Yes Vote (on chain: yes 20, 1 voter)
UI: Finalize & Pick Winner after the vote closed (on chain: rejected, 1 voter is under the quorum of 2)
Script: update_config: voting period 40 s, timelock 0, quorum 2 voters (defaults are 7 days and 10 voters)
Script: B stakes 100 while holding 0 gov tokens (stake_tokens moves no tokens)
Script: update_config: voting period 150 s (so a person clicking through the UI has time to vote); confirmed with solana confirm after the client timed out
evidence.functional_evidence: stake_tokens and buy_tokens move no tokens and no SOL (the transfers are commented-out placeholders), so voting power is free and the treasury path does not run.

limitations: stake_tokens and buy_tokens move no tokens and no SOL (the transfers are commented-out placeholders), so voting power is free: anyone can give themselves any amount up to the treasury's counter.
Quorum is an absolute count of unique voters (config.quorum_percentage, default 10), not a percentage.
We set the voting period to 40 s for the script and 150 s for the UI run, timelock 0 and quorum 2 (defaults: 7 days and 10 voters) with update_config, which the app has no screen for.
The proposal page's live counts come from a websocket log feed; on a plain HTTP RPC they stay at 0 until you reload, while the chain has the votes.
Only the DAO authority can finalize; on sol.college that is the test wallet m4Ac…, so other visitors can vote but not finalize.
